verification_report.summary: The proof is correct, conditional exactly as stated on the canonical-collar bridge. The source-localization lemma uses only legal analytic moment blocks, preserves boundary avoidance under concatenation, and gives the required proper open localization and zero extension. Refined branch valuations agree with closed-point orders on the residual curve; virtual-annulus monomialization gives one common expansion index, exact primitive rays, and finite branch separation. The repaired elementary-star construction retains all virtual-disc branches, cuts only finitely many annular components, and, after a second localization retaining the separating block, proves the global-in-U exact preimage identity for every selected canonical collar. The rigid zero-atom lemma correctly uses a finite-flat disc tube and radial cutoffs with uniformly bounded d'd'' total variation. The Euclidean matrix-current calculation yields constant edge fluxes, full-star balancing, and no positive vertex remainder. Type-3 balancing and the type-2 residual-divisor argument force the ordinary/calibrated flux ratio to be constant; Riemann--Roch over the actual residual field shows the relevant nonnegative principal-invariant divisor functionals are multiples of degree. Connectivity and tropical-dimension-zero vanishing then globalize T=c delta_Y. Finite normalization, the locally finite rigid conductor set, and the fundamental-cycle identity give the reduced-curve classification. Finally, componentwise curvature equality follows because the remaining signed measures are supported on a locally finite rigid set and have no atoms, proving the stated continuous-psh Bedford--Taylor independence. All cited CLD, Ducros, and Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff statements were checked in their primary sources with matching definitions and hypotheses.
